title: PALA: Plateau-Aware Learning with Adaptive Memory Faster Convergence via SNR-Guided Plateau Classification and Cosine Bounce Restarts for Adam-Family Optimizers
abstract: PALA (Plateau-Aware Learning with Adaptive Memory) matches ReduceLROnPlateau in final accuracywhile using 25% fewer training epochs, reaching competitive accuracy 13 epochs sooner and early-stopping ata mean of 75 epochs versus 100 for all fixed-schedule baselines. This convergence efficiency is PALA’s primarypractical contribution: the same validation accuracy for a quarter less GPU compute, with no schedule-specifichyperparameter tuning.PALA achieves this by diagnosing why a model has stalled, not merely that it has stalled, and respondingwith a geometry-adapted escape strategy. It reads the first and second Adam moments already maintained bythe optimizer at zero additional cost: the gradient signal-to-noise ratio SNR = ∥E[g]∥/∥E[g2]1/2∥ and thegradient variance proxy GVar = E[∥v1/2t ∥] are jointly mapped through a threshold classifier to one of threelandscape categories (SADDLE, FLAT, or SHARP), each triggering a type-specific cosine learning-rate bounce. Aregion-of-interest (ROI) memory accumulates (floor_lr, loss_gain, plateau_type) triples acrossbounces; the next floor is selected by a recency–ROI weighted mean over type-matched entries. Adaptive β2scaling accelerates second-moment adaptation during bounces, and a β1 reduction on saddle exits increasesgradient direction reactivity. A gradient-agreement detector escalates bounce amplitude when the optimizerre-enters the same trap. On CIFAR-100 (PalaCNN) and STL-10, PALA outperforms plain Adam by +3.8 pp onaverage and matches ReduceLROnPlateau to within 0.2 pp in final accuracy. Our ablation further reveals thata more aggressive floor decay (γ=0.1) yields 63.3%, surpassing ReduceLROnPlateau (62.0%) by 1.3 pp.On ResNet-18, PALA underperforms in the 100-epoch regime due to BatchNorm’s suppression of gradientvariance signals.

abstract: BU145-A, “Formal Handshake Interface Network under B_U: Four Pillars, Four Mechanism Engines, and the B_U Interface Topology,” establishes the formal-system handshake interface as a structured network between B_U and downstream formal domains. Its central object is the complete interface map formed by BU108–117 and BU123–128. These sixteen files are not treated as isolated essays or field-specific analogies. They are organized as a coherent network through which formal systems, mathematical structures, verification procedures, recovery mechanisms, semantic mappings, distributed protocols, and combinatorial boundaries can be brought back into B_U’s chain of admissibility, weak persistence, residual stratification, friction-cost accounting, feedback compatibility, and settlement standing. The paper’s first organizing layer is the four-pillar structure: categorical semantics, formal verification, distributed fault tolerance, and combinatorial optimization. Categorical semantics handles structure preservation, semantic equivalence, transport mapping, type inhabitation, invariant kernels, and quotient-preserving transformations. Formal verification handles exact certification, proof admissibility, benchmark validity, formal verification, zero-error recovery, and settlement-compatible validity. Distributed fault tolerance handles deterministic partial views, distributed consistency, local recovery, replica divergence, synchronization cost, and distributed recovery. Combinatorial optimization handles matroid realizability, matroid-rank boundary, statistical sufficiency, minimal determining sets, rank limits, independence structures, and polynomially constrained recovery. These four pillars describe the application-level topology of the formal handshake network. The second organizing layer is the four-mechanism-engine structure: information-theoretic bounds, matroid and linear-algebraic tools, distributed local computation, and group/closure symmetry. These engines describe how local formal information can be transformed into globally recoverable, verifiable, and behavior-preserving structure. Information-theoretic bounds set recoverability limits, zero-error conditions, capacity constraints, and admissible compression boundaries. Matroid and linear-algebraic tools extract invariant structure through rank, basis, closure, independence, representation, and low-dimensional recovery. Distributed local computation converts partial views, message passing, local checks, and synchronization paths into global consistency or recovery. Group/closure symmetry provides quotient, orbit, stabilizer, closure, canonical representative, and equivalence-class structures that preserve sameness across semantic shells. BU145-A then aligns the two layers. The four pillars identify where formal systems operate; the four mechanism engines identify how formal systems convert local readouts into global recoverability. Under B_U, both layers are reclassified through a single structural chain: \text{local readout}\rightarrow\text{invariant extraction}\rightarrow\text{bounded transformation}\rightarrow\text{globally verifiable recovery}\rightarrowK_{\min}^{formal}\rightarrow\text{settlement-compatible standing}. The final judgment is that BU108–117 and BU123–128 form a high-connectivity interface network rather than a collection of separate formal topics. Their shared function is to prevent formal systems from drifting into self-contained symbolic closure. A formal structure gains B_U-compatible force only when its proof, recovery, equivalence, semantic fidelity, invariant kernel, transport, rank boundary, distributed state, and verification path can be mapped to admissibility, residual discipline, cost, feedback, and settlement. BU145-A therefore functions as the interface topology file: it shows how B_U can handshake with formal systems without surrendering source-axis hierarchy, standing boundaries, or reality-settlement discipline. BU145-B, “Three Closure Modules of the Formal Handshake Interface under B_U,” establishes the closure-theorem layer of the B_U formal handshake interface. While BU145-A maps the formal interface network across four application pillars and four mechanism engines, BU145-B advances the network into three sealing modules: Information-Theoretic Bounds under B_U, Quotient-Orbit-Closure Symmetry under B_U, and Local-to-Global Verifiable Recovery under B_U. Its central purpose is to prevent the formal handshake network from remaining a loose collection of field-specific correspondences. The paper compresses the entire interface into a single structural chain: local information enters a bounded formal window, invariant content is extracted, transformation is constrained, recovery becomes globally verifiable, and the resulting structure is tested for settlement-compatible standing under B_U. The first closure module, Information-Theoretic Bounds under B_U, defines recoverability limits, zero-error conditions, capacity constraints, compression boundaries, and verification ceilings as formal expressions of admissibility boundaries. Information theory determines what can be distinguished, transmitted, recovered, compressed, or certified under finite resources. B_U relocates these bounds into the standing chain: a capacity result, zero-error limit, or rank bound gains structural force when it identifies a real admissibility boundary, exposes friction cost, and prevents unsupported recovery claims from entering settlement. The module links Shannon capacity, zero-error capacity, rank constraints, entropy limits, and recoverability thresholds to C_{fric}, \Delta I, and standing discipline. The second closure module, Quotient-Orbit-Closure Symmetry under B_U, seals the equivalence and representation side of formal systems. Quotients, orbits, closures, stabilizers, canonical representatives, normal forms, invariant kernels, and closure-invariant classifiers are treated as mechanisms for preserving the same admissible object across semantic shells, transformations, presentations, and domains. B_U classifies this module as the structural discipline that prevents vocabulary substitution, symbolic relabeling, or representation change from simulating true equivalence. A quotient is valid when it preserves the standing-bearing structure; an orbit is meaningful when it tracks admissible variation; a closure is legitimate when it preserves the boundary of the recoverable object. The third closure module, Local-to-Global Verifiable Recovery under B_U, establishes the mother theorem of the file. Local readouts, partial views, distributed observations, algebraic invariants, semantic invariants, and bounded transformations can support global recovery only when they preserve the same admissible structure through residual audit, friction-cost exposure, feedback compatibility, and settlement. The module links deterministic partial view, zero-error recovery, matroid-rank boundary, distributed recovery, semantic fidelity, invariant kernel, and transport mapping into one recovery chain. The final judgment is that formal systems obtain B_U-compatible force through three closures: information-theoretic boundaries define what can be recovered, quotient-orbit-closure symmetry defines what remains the same, and local-to-global verifiable recovery defines when partial readouts become globally settleable. BU145-B therefore functions as the closure-theorem layer of the formal handshake interface: it seals the path from local formal structure to settlement-compatible standing.

title: From Planning to Execution: An Integrated Approach
abstract: Abstract Digitalization in the upstream oil and gas industry has received much attention and efforts during the last decades, resulting in improved processes and information flow. However, the focus has mostly been on vertical digital integrations: at a given stage in a well life-cycle (WLC), the involved actors can often use standardized APIs and data models to ease the communication and collaboration, but horizontal integration remains difficult. The Exchange of information between the successive steps of the WLC is challenging because of the differences in processes and workflows at these different stages. We propose in this paper an approach to perform the horizontal integration between the well planning and the execution steps, where the execution is assumed to be autonomous. The approach is based on the observation that the simulations involved in the risk analysis and operational planning stages are very similar to the ones required to train an autonomous drilling agent. We propose to leverage these similarities and isolate a component, common to the two operations, that can serve as a direct link between planning and execution. This component is the control architecture used to both perform planning simulations, train and agent and actually execute the autonomous drilling policy. We explain in this article how planning and execution can be seen as a single, continuous workflow and discuss the benefits and challenges of this approach. Then, we define an autonomous drilling control architecture that can be used in both stages of the workflow. We explain how it can be used during the planning process for combined risk and performance analysis and optimal policy determination, and during the execution to control the actual process. The proposed architecture is based on hierarchical state machines. The hierarchical feature accounts for the heterogeneity of decisions leading to autonomous operations. The different levels of decision making can make the computational cost of policy optimization prohibitive: we therefore introduce a high level of modularity that allows to treat the various decision problems independently. Finally, we discuss the potential of using hierarchical state machines for automated system analysis and testing.

title: Beyond Linear Activation Steering: Invertible Latent Transformations for Controlling LLM Behavior
abstract: Activation steering provides a lightweight inference-time mechanism for controlling large language models (LLMs) by modifying their internal activation vectors toward desired behaviors. Most existing methods compute a fixed steering direction in the original activation space, typically from pairs of contrastive examples using mean differences, linear probes, or arbitrary separability criteria. While effective to a certain extent, these methods treat behavioral control as a global, linear, additive offset: the same direction is applied across inputs, and behaviors are linearly separable. This can be restrictive when behavioral features vary nonlinearly across the activation space or lie on curved and anisotropic manifolds, where the optimal intervention may be input-dependent. To address this limitation, we propose INNSteer, a nonlinear activation steering framework based on invertible latent transformations. Rather than searching for a better steering vector in the original representation space, INNSteer learns a lightweight invertible neural network $ϕ$ that maps an LLM's activations into a latent space where behavioral classes are more amenable to linear control. At inference time, activations are mapped through $ϕ$, steered in the latent space, and mapped back through the exact inverse transformation $ϕ^{-1}$. This makes a simple latent-space translation become a nonlinear, input-dependent intervention in the original activation space. Across experiment settings on multiple LLM families, scales, behavioral traits, and safety benchmarks, INNSteer consistently improves model control over linear, transport-based, and nonlinear steering baselines while largely preserving generation fluency.

title: Ghosted Layers: Unconstrained Activation Alignment for Recovering Layer-Pruned LLMs
abstract: Layer pruning removes entire Transformer decoder blocks from large language models, but introduces a mismatch between the hidden state received by the next surviving layer and the distribution it was trained to process, leading to significant performance degradation. We propose Ghosted Layers, a training-free recovery module that addresses this issue by solving a boundary activation alignment problem. Our method derives a closed-form optimal linear operator from a small calibration set to reconstruct the activation discrepancy introduced by the pruned layers. We show that this solution corresponds to the unconstrained optimum of the alignment objective, whereas existing methods are restricted to constrained solutions over limited operator subspaces. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and pruning strategies demonstrate that our method consistently improves accuracy and perplexity over prior training-free baselines, while preserving the efficiency gains of layer pruning. Official code repository: https://github.com/daniel-eai/ghosted_layers_official_repository/.

title: The SQU, TriQ, and SevenQ: Standard Hardware for the Origami ISA
abstract: CORRECTION NOTICE (2026-08). The figure "4.3× directed magic-routing efficiency", quoted three times and attributed to a companion paper, does not appear in that paper. It is unsourced and should be disregarded. A revised version is in preparation. The Origami Instruction Set Architecture (O-ISA) was introduced alongside a conjectural exotic hardware substrate — the Resonance Processing Unit (RPU) — requiring non-associative materials to support octonion computation. This paper establishes that the base Origami ISA requires no exotic hardware whatsoever. It runs today on any quantum processor supporting three-qubit gates: superconducting transmons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, and photonic chips. Two complementary architectural primitives are specified. The TriQ (Origami Triple) is the fundamental three-qubit register: three physical qubits in Fano-plane incidence connectivity, corresponding to one logical qubit in the [[7,1,3]] Steane code. The SQU (Symplectic Quantum Unit) is the full processor architecture built from TriQ registers, with the Magic-ISA opcode set and inter-register typed routing. The SevenQ is the complete seven-qubit Fano register: all seven points of PG(2,2) simultaneously realised, corresponding to the full [[7,1,3]] Steane code with its six gauge degrees of freedom corresponding bijectively to the six non-classical Fano orbit valences. The key diagnostic opcode is ORBIT: seven simultaneous Pauli measurements returning the Fano orbit valence label of the register state, replacing the conjectured Freudenthal determinant ALU with seven standard readout operations. The SQU achieves fault-tolerant universal quantum computation with 7 physical qubits per logical qubit for CS-family gates via gauge-orbit selection, and 15 for CCZ gates via code switch — both at zero magic-state distillation overhead. A critical non-obvious result: SevenQ ORBIT is identical to standard Steane syndrome extraction. The seven syndrome measurements already performed at every error correction cycle are the ORBIT opcode, with the orbit valence label computed in classical post-processing at zero additional hardware cost. Three hardware tiers are defined: SQU (standard qubits, available today), SQU-diode (6-7 directed Fano coupling topology, near-term), and RPU (non-associative materials, long-term). The SevenQ-diode variant applies the 6-7 broken-symmetry topology to the full seven-qubit register for directed magic routing at 4× symmetric efficiency. The paper also establishes the exploration order for the projective tower: TriQ (3 qubits, minimal n=3) → SevenQ (7 qubits, complete n=3) → 1531-Anvil (15 qubits, first n=4). title: GCF: A Token-Optimized Wire Format for Structured LLM Interactions
abstract: GCF is an AI-native wire format for structured data in LLM systems. 2,400+ evaluations across 11 models and 3 providers. 43 billion+ lossless round-trips across 5 formats. Two published papers. Comprehension: 100% accuracy on every frontier model on standard workloads. 91.2% on structurally complex data where JSON drops to 53.4% and TOON to 68.2%. No model has ever been trained on GCF. Token efficiency: 50-92% fewer tokens than JSON (50-69% per call, up to 92% with session deduplication). JSON overhead is 81% structural noise at scale; GCF overhead is 0.2%. Tokenizer safety: GCF's grammar characters were selected from the set empirically verified to have near-zero merge rates across 43 tokenizers from 20 providers. Pipe delimiter: 0.47% merge rate, 24 mergeable words. JSON: 8.17%, 1,939 mergeable words. TOON tab: 32.91%, 1,238 mergeable words. A controlled experiment proves delimiter choice matters at the transformer level: models trained with merge barriers on delimiter characters develop 4.6x more structural attention heads, achieve 3x better structured data comprehension and 3-5x better code comprehension, with zero natural language cost. title: Advanced Actor-Critic for Caesarii-Style Auto Pipe Stress Ananlysis
abstract: Abstract This study presents an Advanced Actor-Critic (AAC) reinforcement-learning framework for automating linear support-type selection in piping stress analysis for shipbuilding and offshore systems. In practice, improper support configurations often result in excessive stress, displacement, or nozzle loads, leading to repeated manual redesign cycles. The proposed framework aims to reduce these iterations by learning consistent and code-compliant support-type decisions directly from analysis feedback. The AAC framework enhances a Vanilla Actor-Critic (VAC) structure through domain-driven improvements that stabilize learning and improve adaptability across thermal and mechanical load cases. These include adaptive advantage control, stabilized long-horizon reward evaluation, retention of effective behaviors under changing operating conditions, and modeling of interactions among distributed supports within the piping configuration. Applications to cryogenic and high-temperature piping systems show that the trained policy reduces redesign iterations and improves first-pass structural code compliance compared with a VAC baseline. The framework provides stable, interpretable, and practically deployable support-type decisions for automated piping stress design.

title: CADFit: Precise Mesh-to-CAD Program Generation with Hybrid Optimization
abstract: Despite recent progress, recovering parametric CAD construction sequences from geometric input, such as meshes or point clouds, is a key challenge for design and manufacturing, as existing CAD reconstruction and generation methods are largely restricted to difficult-to-edit formats like meshes or Breps or editable simple sketch-and-extrude pipelines and low-complexity datasets. We introduce CADFit, a hybrid optimization-based CAD reconstruction framework that recovers complex, editable CAD construction sequences from meshes by incrementally fitting and validating parametric operations using geometric feedback. Our approach is distinguished by formulating reconstruction as an IoU-driven optimization over structured CAD programs and supporting a rich set of operations, including extrusions, revolutions, fillets, and chamfers. Experiments on multiple CAD benchmarks show that CADFit outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-to-CAD methods in volumetric Intersection-over-Union and Chamfer Distance, while substantially reducing the Invalid Ratio of reconstructed CAD programs, particularly for complex designs. We further present a multimodal pipeline that enables end-to-end reconstruction of CAD construction sequences from images by combining image-based geometry reconstruction with CADFit. By enabling accurate reconstruction of higher-complexity CAD models, CADFit provides a practical foundation for generating richer datasets and advancing future learning-based approaches to CAD reverse engineering. The code is available at: https://github.com/ghadinehme/CADFit.

title: DUBAI Theory: Digit Unified Binary Analysis & Indexing — A Polar-Geometric Fingerprint for Sub-Linear Integer Search
abstract: We present DUBAI (Digit Unified Binary Analysis & Indexing), a novel multi-layer structural fingerprinting framework for sub-linear integer search, inspired by biological fingerprint classification principles (whorl, loop, arch). The framework transforms integers into geometric entities within a 10-sector polar coordinate system ($\Delta\theta = 36^\circ$). By leveraging advanced structural layers—including a unique Shading Layer bounded by the maximum and terminal digits, and a Combined Distance Layer fusing linear digit sums with polar-geometric displacement—DUBAI achieves empirical candidate set filtration rates between 99.956% and 100% across various real-world datasets, including UAE phone numbers, national IDs, and stock prices. A hybrid DUBAI+Hash variant achieves global rank #3 in search speed performance without requiring pre-sorted input. This preprint establishes the theoretical foundations, formal propositions, empirical benchmarks, and documented distribution-specific limitations of the DUBAI framework.

title: Sistema Adaptativo Educacional Baseado na Combinação de Dimensões da Aprendizagem
abstract: Resumo Sistemas adaptativos educacionais buscam personalizar experiências de aprendizagem conforme as características dos estudantes. Entretanto, muitas abordagens concentram-se em indicadores de desempenho acadêmico, explorando de forma limitada outras dimensões da aprendizagem. Neste contexto, esta pesquisa de mestrado investiga como a combinação de dimensões cognitivas, metacognitivas e afetivas influencia a personalização de trilhas. Para isso, foi desenvolvido um modelo baseado em lógica fuzzy que integra desempenho, percepção de dificuldade e autoconfiança para recomendar trilhas de Reforço, Regular ou Desafio. A pesquisa está estruturada em três etapas: mapeamento sistemático da literatura, avaliação em um curso presencial de Robótica com Arduino e aplicação em um curso on-line de Fundamentos de IA Generativa. Os resultados indicam a viabilidade da abordagem proposta e o potencial de modelos multidimensionais para apoiar a personalização da aprendizagem.

title: Knowledge Graph–Based Modeling and Reuse of Coating Process Knowledge for Cruise Ship Section
abstract: Abstract Coating is a critical process in cruise ship construction, directly affecting corrosion resistance, surface quality, and lifecycle performance. However, coating knowledge in shipyards is often fragmented across heterogeneous data sources, limiting structured management and reuse. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a task-oriented and temporally aware knowledge graph framework for modeling and integrating ship block coating process knowledge. A temporal process knowledge graph is formally defined based on multi-source data analysis, combining ontology-based schema construction with data-driven instantiation. Engineering documents are processed through table mapping and a RoBERTa-based joint entity–relation extraction model to generate structured process and semantic subgraphs. An entity alignment–based fusion method integrating graph convolutional structural embeddings and textual similarity is further developed to unify heterogeneous knowledge sources. Experimental results on both benchmark and domain-specific datasets demonstrate superior performance over representative baselines. The resulting unified knowledge graph enables structured representation, traceability, and reuse of coating process knowledge, supporting intelligent process management and digital transformation in cruise ship manufacturing.

title: Operationalizing Linguistic Methods through Prompt-Engineering Skills: An Automatic Chinese Web Neologism Detection Pipeline
abstract: We present a method for automatic Chinese web neologism detection that operationalizes traditional linguistic identification principles as prompt-engineering skills. The method has four stages: tokenizer-independent character n-gram candidate generation; dictionary anchoring with a Pointwise Mutual Information pre-filter; a well-formedness skill based on Chinese word-formation principles; and a combined rule and three-way classification skill that distinguishes neologism, entity, and none. Applied to the BAAI CCI 3.0 corpus (267M documents), the method produces 226,959 classified candidates including 4,853 labeled neologisms. To evaluate the method, we develop a per-stage conditional recall decomposition in which the pipeline's strict recall factors mathematically into the product of stage conditional recalls. Applied to Hou (2023) (4,199 entries), the decomposition exposes Stage 1 candidate coverage and Stage 4B LLM semantic judgment as the two bottlenecks (R=41.5% and 60.0% respectively), while intermediate stages are near-lossless. A length-stratified analysis further reveals that the structural well-formedness skill is length-invariant (>= 96.9%) whereas the semantic novelty-classification skill is length-dependent (65.6%/59.0%/44.1% across 2/3/4-character candidates), mapping a current boundary of skill-based linguistic operationalization. We release the method, pipeline outputs, and evaluation protocol as public resources.

title: Relational Epipolar Graphs for Robust Relative Camera Pose Estimation
abstract: A key component of Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) is estimating relative camera poses using matched keypoints. Accurate estimation is challenged by noisy correspondences. Classical methods rely on stochastic hypothesis sampling and iterative estimation, while learning-based methods often lack explicit geometric structure. In this work, we reformulate relative pose estimation as a relational inference problem over epipolar correspondence graphs, where matched keypoints are nodes and nearby ones are connected by edges. Graph operations such as pruning, message passing, and pooling estimate a quaternion rotation, translation vector, and the Essential Matrix (EM). Minimizing a loss comprising (i) L_2 differences with ground truth (GT), (ii) Frobenius norm between estimated and GT EMs, (iii) singular value differences, (iv) heading angle differences, and (v) scale differences, yields the relative pose between image pairs. The dense detector-free method LoFTR is used for matching. Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show improved robustness to dense noise and large baseline variation compared to classical and learning-guided approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of global relational consensus.

title: Automated breast cancer cell counting: comparing multi-class segmentation and two-stage classification strategies
abstract: The manual interpretation of Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) histopathology images for breast cancer diagnosis is hindered by time limitations and observer bias. This research seeks to create an automated system using Deep Learning for cell detection and classification, evaluating two key approaches: Multi-class Segmentation (single-stage) and Segmentation followed by Classification (two-stage). U-Net architecture was employed for segmentation, while MobileNetV2 and VGG16 were used for classification. The models were tested on the public IHC4BC dataset and primary data from Airlangga University Hospital (RSUA). The study also evaluated the impact of Resizing versus Tiling data processing strategies. Experimental results showed that while MobileNetV2 and VGG16 classification models achieved a high testing accuracy of 98.80%, the two-stage integrated system revealed a high counting error with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 119.87 for positive cells, primarily due to under-segmentation of overlapping cells. In contrast, the Multi-class Segmentation approach utilizing the Tiling strategy demonstrated superior performance. This model effectively preserved spatial resolution and distinguished cell types simultaneously, achieving the lowest positive cell MAE of 18.46 and a negative cell MAE of 1.66. This study concluded that multi-class segmentation with a Tiling strategy was the most effective and accurate approach for automated cell counting in histopathology images.

title: Adaptive Lidar-Radar Data Fusion for Enhanced Surface Target State Estimation in Maritime Environments
abstract: Abstract Reliable perception is essential for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) operating in complex and dynamic maritime environments. Adaptive LiDAR–Radar data fusion for USVs in maritime environments is investigated in this study. The perception system is modeled by fusing LiDAR and radar data using Dempster–Shafer (D-S) evidence theory, where basic probability assignments (BPAs) are constructed for each sensor and their weights are adaptively adjusted according to data quality. Experimental validation is performed in realistic waterway scenarios near the Yangtze River, and the results are compared with single-sensor perception methods to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The fusion method demonstrates enhanced robustness and reliability, achieving more stable surface target detection and state estimation. These findings highlight the advantage of adaptive multi-sensor fusion in complex maritime perception tasks.

title: A complete characterization of a family of permutation trinomials over $\mathbb F_{p^2}$
abstract: Let $p>3$ be a prime and let $$f_{λ_1,λ_2}(x)=x^{p^2-p+1}+λ_1x^{p^2}+λ_2x^{2p-1}\in\mathbb F_{p^2}[x].$$ We determine all pairs $(λ_1,λ_2)\in(\mathbb F_{p^2})^2$ for which $f_{λ_1,λ_2}$ is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb F_{p^2}$. The final classification consists of three explicit families. The first one is the binomial case $λ_1=0$. The other two are obtained from the condition $λ_2=cλ_1^3$, with $c\in \mathbb F_{p}^{*}$, and are defined by two simple equations involving the norm $λ_1^{p+1}$. The proof is based on the AGW criterion and on the study of a quartic curve naturally associated with the rational function induced on the unit circle $μ_{p+1}$.

The final classification consists of three explicit families. The first one is the binomial case $λ_1=0$. The other two are obtained from the condition $λ_2=cλ_1^3$, with $c\in \mathbb F_{p}^{*}$, and are defined by two simple equations involving the norm $λ_1^{p+1}$. title: Know More, Know Clearer: A Meta-Cognitive Framework for Knowledge Augmentation in Large Language Models
abstract: Knowledge augmentation has significantly enhanced the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive tasks. However, existing methods typically operate on the simplistic premise that model performance equates with internal knowledge, overlooking the knowledge-confidence gaps that lead to overconfident errors or uncertain truths. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel meta-cognitive framework for reliable knowledge augmentation via differentiated intervention and alignment. Our approach leverages internal cognitive signals to partition the knowledge space into mastered, confused, and missing regions, guiding targeted knowledge expansion. Furthermore, we introduce a cognitive consistency mechanism to synchronize subjective certainty with objective accuracy, ensuring calibrated knowledge boundaries. Extensive experiments demonstrate the our framework consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating its rationality in not only enhancing knowledge capabilities but also fostering cognitive behaviors that better distinguish knowns from unknowns. All codes are available at https://github.com/AI9Stars/Know-More-Know-Clearer.

title: An Optimisation Model for Umbilical Cable Design Considering Elements of Different Functions, Materials and Sizes With Possible Layering Restrictions
abstract: Abstract This work presents an optimisation algorithm for the accommodation of functional components within the cross-section of umbilical cables. The proposed approach efficiently handles the coexistence of components with differing radii, while also allowing for the imposition of predefined layering constraints. The algorithm combines a gradient-based method for minimising the objective function with a flexible implementation of layering rules and a proper consideration of geometric constraints, ensuring the avoidance of component interference and the preservation of radial symmetry. To reduce the risk of convergence to local minima, multiple randomly generated initial configurations are employed, followed by an iterative competition process in which the best-performing solution is retained at each solver iteration. Six different representative layering constraints are examined, together with their corresponding optimised configurations. The results demonstrate ability of the algorithm to correctly accommodate these constraints and illustrate their impact in terms of the increased filler area required in the resulting cross-sectional layouts.

title: What Makes a Desired Graph for Relational Deep Learning?
abstract: Relational deep learning (RDL) converts relational databases (RDBs) into heterogeneous graphs, but graphs derived directly from database schemas are often not well suited for how graph neural networks (GNNs) perform relational reasoning. We study what makes a relational graph suitable for deep learning and show that schema-derived graphs suffer from two systematic failures: information overload and semantic fragmentation. Our empirical analysis reveals that the desired graph is not the raw schema, but a result of controlled structural adaptation. Performance depends on balancing two operations: mitigating information overload via filtering, and repairing semantic fragmentation via injection. Specifically, filtering serves as a bias-variance knob with non-monotonic effects, while injection improves performance only when it explicitly restores the relational dependencies missing from the original schema. Based on these findings, we develop an end-to-end structural optimizer that applies both operations to adapt relational graphs automatically. Across 26 tasks spanning classification, regression, and recommendation, the optimized graphs consistently improve accuracy while often reducing inference cost.

title: Zero-Flow Encoders
abstract: Flow-based methods have achieved significant success in various generative modeling tasks, capturing nuanced details within complex data distributions. However, few existing works have exploited this unique capability to resolve fine-grained structural details beyond generation tasks. This paper presents a flow-inspired framework for representation learning. First, we demonstrate that a rectified flow trained using independent coupling is zero everywhere at t=0.5 if and only if the source and target distributions are identical. We term this property the zero-flow criterion. Second, we show that this criterion can certify conditional independence, thereby extracting sufficient information from the data. Third, we translate this criterion into a tractable, simulation-free loss function that enables learning amortized Markov blankets in graphical models and latent representations in self-supervised learning tasks. Experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. The code reproducing our experiments can be found at: https://github.com/probabilityFLOW/zfe.

title: Role of CMOS Control Electronics in Quantum Computing Systems
abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a promising computational paradigm capable of solving certain problems beyond the practical capabilities of classical computers. Although quantum processors rely on quantum mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement but their operation depends heavily on classical electronic systems for control, communication, and measurement. Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) technology plays a critical role in providing this electronic infrastructure due to its low power consumption, scalability, and high integration density. This paper explores the role of CMOS-based control electronics in superconducting quantum computing systems and the functions of key components including Arbitrary Waveform Generators (AWGs), Digital-to-Analog Converters (DACs), mixers, transmission lines, resonators, and readout circuits. The paper also examines the emerging field of Cryogenic CMOS (Cryo-CMOS), which aims to improve scalability and reduce latency in future quantum computers. The study highlights how CMOS technology acts as a bridge between classical electronics and quantum hardware.

title: Explainable Optimization: A Call for Interdisciplinary Action
abstract: Operations research and management science models support decisions that affect patients, workers, citizens, and public institutions. Decision-makers, such as clinicians approving surgical schedules, planners allocating disaster relief resources, or managers designing workforce rotations, increasingly require clear and actionable justifications that bridge the gap between mathematical optimization outputs and the intuitive reasoning stakeholders need to trust, contest, and implement recommended decisions. Yet the field has traditionally evaluated optimization models through computational criteria such as feasibility, optimality, scalability, and solution time, while treating explanation as a secondary concern. Mathematical transparency, provided through access to objectives, constraints, shadow prices, or sensitivity reports, does not automatically offer the forms of justification that stakeholders need to understand, trust, contest, or implement optimization-based decisions. This paper calls for the development of explainable optimization (XOpt) as a distinct interdisciplinary area that moves beyond algorithmic efficiency and incorporates behavioral, cognitive, and pragmatic perspectives to address this explanatory deficit.

abstract: One of the challenges of working on R-universe is that there is never really a release day. Unlike software projects that accumulate changes for a big launch, R-universe evolves continuously. New features, infrastructure improvements, UI tweaks, and build system enhancements are silently deployed all the time without most people noticing. Every now and then, however, a few features emerge that are worth highlighting.

title: Recursive Intelligence: Human-AI Synergy and the Economics of Emergence
abstract: The economics of artificial intelligence is built on a foundation that is not merely incomplete. It is wrong. And every cost-benefit analysis, organizational design decision, and governance framework constructed on top of it inherits that error in full. The two dominant frameworks, labor substitution and productivity augmentation, are organized around the wrong unit of analysis. Both treat AI as an input and humans as operators. Neither accounts for what actually happens when humans and AI systems engage in sustained iterative interaction: the emergence of intelligence, insight, and value that neither party could have produced independently, and that no conventional production function can model or measure. This paper advances two central claims. The first is that Human-AI Synergy, the recursive iterative co-production of human and artificial intelligence, constitutes a distinct economic category that existing frameworks cannot model or measure. The second is more provocative and more consequential: properly structured iterative human-AI collaboration does not merely make humans more productive. It makes them cognitively more capable, more creative, and more innovative. This is not a marginal efficiency gain. It is an expansion of the human cognitive frontier itself, a testable proposition that directly inverts the dominant cultural narrative and demands a new economic framework to analyze, measure, and govern. The failure to theorize recursive human-AI co-production is not a gap in the literature. It is a systematic misspecification with measurable consequences for how we design organizations, govern technology, and calculate what AI is actually worth.

title: Percepción del consumidor sobre el uso de la Inteligencia Artificial en el marketing empresarial
abstract: La inteligencia artificial se ha convertido en una herramienta que está cada vez más presente en las estrategias empresariales, transformando especialmente la forma en que las empresas se relacionan con sus clientes a través del marketing. Sin embargo, más allá de sus aplicaciones técnicas, resulta relevante preguntarse cómo la perciben quienes la experimentan desde el otro lado: los consumidores. En este trabajo, el objetivo es estudiar en qué medida la población es consciente del uso que las empresas hacen de la IA, qué valoración le dan en términos de confianza, privacidad y ética, y si está relacionada con el comportamiento de compra. Para ello, se han revisado los fundamentos teóricos de la IA en el entorno empresarial, sus principales aplicaciones en el marketing y casos reales de implantación en empresas de referencia. Posteriormente, se ha llevado a cabo un estudio basado en un cuestionario dirigido a consumidores, que ha sido complementado con la perspectiva de siete profesionales del sector con presencia internacional. Los datos se han analizado mediante diversas pruebas con el objetivo de identificar patrones y tendencias que permitiesen extraer conclusiones sobre la relación entre empresa, tecnología y consumidor en el contexto actual.

title: Fast and Robust On-Device Speaker Diarization: Relative Minimum Cluster Size for Stride-Accelerated Pipelines
abstract: Speech applications such as meeting transcription and voice agents would benefit from on-device speaker diarization, but practical adoption is limited by inference cost. We study how far a Pyannote 3.1-based pipeline can be accelerated on consumer hardware (an RTX 5070 Ti GPU and an Apple M4 laptop) while preserving diarization error rate (DER). A simple recipe: coarser segmentation stride and per-chunk embedding, yields multi-fold speedups and is DER-neutral on AMI, but degrades sharply on in-the-wild data: on VoxConverse, DER rises from 0.075 to 0.113. We trace the failure to speaker under-counting in the clustering stage, caused by a fixed minimum cluster size interacting with the reduced number of embeddings per speaker. We propose a relative minimum cluster size, mcs = round(f * n) with f = 0.01, which adapts to the embedding budget per recording. A single value of f recovers VoxConverse DER to 0.079 (about 89% of the lost accuracy) while keeping AMI flat, and the accelerated pipeline reaches up to 12.2x speedup on AMI (MPS) over our CAM++ baseline.

title: Hierarchical Memory-Augmented World Models for Long-Horizon Robotic Task Planning in Dynamic Environments
abstract: Long-horizon robotic task planning in dynamic, partially observed environments remains a formidable challenge due to the compounding of uncertainty, the combinatorial explosion of action sequences, and the need for rapid adaptation to unpredictable changes. Hierarchical memory-augmented world models offer a promising architectural response by structuring learned environment models into multiple temporal and spatial scales while equipping each level with dedicated memory components. This paper presents a system-level analysis of such architectures, emphasizing structural trade-offs between representational fidelity, memory capacity, planning depth, and computational tractability. We examine how hierarchical decomposition can decouple abstract task reasoning from fine-grained control, how external and action-aware memory modules can stabilize long-context predictions, and how these elements collectively support robustness in open-world deployments. The discussion extends beyond algorithmic design to encompass governance, fairness, sustainability, and infrastructure requirements, drawing on cross-domain comparisons from cloud robotics, large-scale machine learning systems, and socio-technical policy frameworks. We argue that the fusion of hierarchical organization with memory augmentation constitutes a foundational design principle for building reliable, scalable, and ethically deployable autonomous robotic agents, and we identify open questions concerning interoperability, auditability, and energy efficiency that must be addressed by the research community.

title: Implication of Artificial Intelligence for Sports Training and Performance for the Development of Sports in India
authors: Prof. MOHD. Tariq Prof. MOHD. Tariq
Alok Kumar Arya Alok Kumar Arya
abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has created new possibilities for the field of sports, especially in a developing and diverse nation like India. AI is transforming how athletes train, how coaches make decisions, and how sports organizations plan long-term development programs. This abstract explains the major implications of AI for improving sports training and athletic performance, and how these technological changes can support the overall development of the sports sector in India. The purpose is to provide a clear, simple, and human-friendly explanation of how AI can help Indian athletes compete at global standards while also strengthening grassroots sports. AI technologies such as motion analysis, wearable sensors, virtual reality (VR), machine learning–based coaching, and predictive performance analytics now allow coaches and athletes to understand physical movements more accurately than ever before. These tools help identify mistakes, reduce injury risks, and create personalized training plans that match each athlete’s strengths and weaknesses. In Indian sports, where access to expert coaching is often limited, AI-based tools can bring high-quality training to rural and semi-urban regions through mobile applications and cloud platforms. As a result, AI has the power to reduce inequality in sports training and promote equal opportunities for talent across the country.

title: Quantum Multispectral UCA: Classical Simulation and C*_Q Convergence
abstract: We simulate Quantum-UCA classically: quantum 1/f amplitude (λ∝1/f), quantum channel models (depolarization, phase damping, amplitude damping, gate errors) and multispectral operation. Three key findings: (1) classical UCA survives quantum channels up to the coherence limit; (2) quantum amplitude (λ∝1/f) has C_spec=0.22 — outside the classical gap, but C_Q lies in (0,1); (3) C_Q(d→∞) converges toward ≈0.72 — close to the classical C_spec=0.745. This supports the hypothesis of a universal meaning gap beyond classical/quantum

title: Graph-Regularized Agentic Context Evolution
abstract: This record contains the non-archival workshop version of “Graph-Regularized Agentic Context Evolution,” accepted to the ACL 2026 SURGeLLM Workshop. The paper introduces GRACE, a framework for long-horizon agentic context evolution that represents evolving textual policies as typed semantic graphs and performs scoped structural validation around modified policy nodes. The work studies policy evolution in a fixed LLM-agent harness under controlled distribution shift and reports that GRACE sustains reliability improvements over the full evolution trajectory.

title: Youtube Content Analyzer
authors: Prof. Allupati Ch. Patro Prof. Allupati Ch. Patro
abstract: The rapid growth of online video-sharing platforms has significantly changed the way people create, share, and consume information. Among these platforms, YouTube has become one of the world's largest and most influential sources of digital content, with millions of videos uploaded and viewed daily. The vast amount of data generated through views, likes, comments, shares, and subscriptions provides valuable insights into audience behavior and content performance. However, manually analyzing this information is time-consuming and often fails to reveal meaningful patterns. Therefore, there is a need for an intelligent system that can automatically collect, analyze, and visualize YouTube data to support effective decision-making. This research presents a YouTube Content Analyzer, a web-based application designed to analyze YouTube videos and channel performance using data analytics and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. The system utilizes the YouTube Data API to retrieve video metadata, channel statistics, user comments, and engagement metrics in real time. The collected data is preprocessed to remove irrelevant information and improve data quality before analysis. The system then performs sentiment analysis on viewer comments to classify audience opinions as positive, negative, or neutral. This helps content creators and organizations better understand viewer reactions and overall audience satisfaction.

title: Hate Speech Analysis Using IndoBERT in YouTube Comments on the 2024 Indonesian Presidential Debate Video
abstract: A Hate speech in the digital political space during election campaigns has the potential to cause polarization and undermine the quality of public discussion. This study analyzes hate speech in YouTube comments related to the five stages of the 2024 Indonesian presidential debate. We used IndoBERT, a Transformer-based language model specifically trained in Indonesian, to classify comments into hate speech and non-hate speech categories. The dataset consists of 38,742 comments collected from official debate videos. The dataset was labeled using a combination of manual annotation (20%) and semi-supervised learning (80%) using a pseudo-labeling approach. Experimental results show that IndoBERT achieved an average accuracy of 89.7% and a macro F1-score of 0.89 across all stages. IndoBERT outperformed baseline models such as mBERT, SVM, and Random Forest. These findings suggest that IndoBERT is more effective in capturing the linguistic nuances and distinctive Indonesian political rhetoric than multilingual or classical models. This study contributes an Indonesian-language political dataset and a comprehensive evaluation of relevant hate speech detection models for further research. Keywords: hate speech, IndoBERT, 2024 presidential debate, semi-supervised learning.

title: ClinicalAligner26AM: A Cross-Lingual Aligner for Dataset Translation; Evidences from the MultiClinCorpus Shared Task
abstract: Word-level cross-lingual alignment is central to annotation projection, translation auditing, and cross-lingual faithfulness estimation, yet existing neural aligners are rarely adapted to specialized domains. In this paper, we introduce ClinicalAligner26AM, a large-context multilingual aligner model for biomedical and clinical text initialized from ClinicalEncoder26AM. Our training recipe is inspired by AWESoME Align. We build our soft alignment target by sharpening with Sinkhorn-Knop optimal transport a cost matrix established for parallel clinical texts and conversations through the fusion of sentence-level, phrase-level, and token-level signals. We distill this sharpened alignment matrix directly into our student aligner, by encouraging its naive cosine-based token similarity scores to match this target. At inference time, we project source-span scores through the learned token alignment matrix and decode the longest valid high-scoring span in the target text, optionally supported by MultiClinNER predictions summarized in Appendix B. We evaluate CA26AM on the MultiClinCorpus shared task, which projects Spanish clinical entity annotations into six target languages. Our two submitted systems ranked respectively first and second across all languages and entity types, with character-weighted F1 scores above 0.95 in nearly all settings.

title: FedTrustAds: A Federated and Explainable Advertising Attribution Framework with Backdoor-Resilient Learning for Privacy-Preserving Social Commerce Ecosystems
abstract: The proliferation of social commerce ecosystems has created an urgent need for advertising attribution systems that respect user privacy while maintaining accuracy, transparency, and robustness against adversarial threats. Existing centralized attribution models collect vast amounts of user interaction data, raising significant privacy concerns and creating single points of failure for malicious attacks. Federated learning offers a promising paradigm for distributed model training without raw data sharing, yet its application to advertising attribution introduces unique challenges: heterogeneous user behavior patterns, non-IID data distributions, and susceptibility to backdoor attacks that can covertly manipulate attribution outcomes. This paper presents FedTrustAds, a federated and explainable advertising attribution framework designed for privacy-preserving social commerce environments. FedTrustAds integrates three core innovations: a hierarchical federated aggregation mechanism that adapts to local data heterogeneity, a post-hoc explainability module that generates per-prediction attribution narratives using integrated gradients and counterfactual reasoning, and a backdoor-resilient learning protocol that combines anomaly detection on client updates with robust aggregation techniques to neutralize poisoning attempts. The framework is positioned within a broader socio-technical infrastructure that includes compliance-by-design content governance, standardized recommendation APIs, and trusted AI commercialization pathways for small and medium businesses. Through a detailed architectural discussion and comparative analysis with existing alternatives, we demonstrate that FedTrustAds achieves strong privacy guarantees, high attribution accuracy, and resilience against state-of-the-art backdoor attacks while preserving interpretability essential for regulatory compliance and advertiser trust. The paper concludes with policy implications and deployment strategies for multi-tenant platforms.

title: A Modular Annotation-Layer Architecture Specification for Abstract-Representation Models (Restricted Working Set)
abstract: This restricted working set contains a modular architecture specification for an annotation layer over a controlled ISO-704 vocabulary, designed to be embedded in abstract-representation models. It specifies a layer specification, an architecture decomposition into encoder, mapper, predictor, and graph-updater modules, and integration patterns for joint-embedding-predictive, latent video/diffusion, large-language-model, and embodied architectures. The work is a descriptive engineering specification; it reports an architectural design and a local test harness; it makes no consciousness or mind-related claims. Offered as a defensive publication establishing prior art; no patent is sought or filed; released under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Living working set under a metadata-refinement convention. title: QUANTUM OPTICS AND FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICS: PHYSICAL LIMITS OF BELL STATE MEASUREMENT EFFICIENCY IN LINEAR-OPTICAL SYSTEMS
abstract: This paper investigates a critical challenge at the intersection of quantum optics and fundamental physics: the strict physical constraints governing Bell state measurement (BSM) efficiency within linear-optical frameworks. Without the integration of ancilla photons, conventional setups relying on standard linear-optical components are bounded by a fundamental efficiency threshold that cannot be exceeded. We conduct an analytical analysis of the physical roots of this barrier using Hong-Ou-Mandel photon interference phenomena and multi-photon state space geometry. Furthermore, this study models advanced physical techniques to break past this threshold, focusing on non-linear optical mediums—such as parametric down-conversion setups—and polarization-entangled ancilla flying qubits. These analytical insights deliver foundational physical parameters necessary for engineering fault-tolerant optical quantum computing networks and scalable quantum internet repeaters.

title: Role of Mathematics in Artificial Intelligence and Computer Applications
abstract: Mathematics is the backbone of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and modern computer applications. AI systems use mathematical concepts such as linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, and optimization to process data, recognize patterns, and make intelligent decisions. These concepts support technologies including machine learning, neural networks, robotics, computer vision, cyber security, and data science. Linear algebra is used for vectors and matrices in neural networks, while calculus supports optimization and model training. Probability and statistics help systems make predictions under uncertainty. Discrete mathematics forms the basis of algorithms, logic, and cryptography. Optimization techniques improve the accuracy and efficiency of intelligent systems. The integration of mathematics with AI and computer science has transformed sectors such as healthcare, education, banking, agriculture, and transportation. Although challenges such as computational complexity, privacy concerns, and ethical issues remain, mathematics continues to drive innovation and technological advancement in AI and computer applications.

title: BU124 Semantic Fidelity under B_U BU124|B_U 体系下的语义保真
abstract: BU124, “Semantic Fidelity under B_U,” formulates semantic fidelity as a B_U-anchored downstream formal reconstruction. Its object is the class of situations in which a representation, translation, model, proof, program, specification, benchmark, protocol, simulation, or formal system claims to preserve the same meaning across transformation. The paper places this claim under the B_U chain of boundary consistency, dynamic completeness, admissible path space, structured pruning, residual gating, weak persistent morphism, friction-cost accounting, feedback compatibility, and settlement standing. Semantic fidelity is therefore treated as a local preservation claim whose structural force depends on whether the semantic boundary is declared, the target meaning is correctly identified, the invariant core survives transformation, residual drift is exposed, transport cost is paid, and the preserved meaning can enter the B_U settlement chain. The central judgment is direct: semantic fidelity requires preserved meaning under admissible transformation. Surface equivalence, symbolic translation, behavioral similarity, denotational agreement, operational correspondence, benchmark-score matching, or proof-level transport can provide local evidence. Durable fidelity requires preservation of the admissible object through boundary, quotient, invariant core, transport stability, residual audit, feedback, and settlement. A representation can look equivalent while its target meaning drifts. A translation can preserve syntax while losing admissible structure. A model can preserve behavior inside a local context while failing under deployment or semantic transport. Under B_U, fidelity becomes structurally meaningful when the same semantic object remains retained across presentation, abstraction, execution, evaluation, and settlement. BU124 develops this handshake through a sequence of definitions: semantic presentation, declared semantic boundary, target meaning, admissible semantic domain, semantic quotient, invariant core, semantic transport, fidelity gap, residual semantic drift, weak persistent semantic path, friction-cost bridge, feedback-confirmed meaning, and settlement-compatible semantic fidelity. These definitions translate the B_U source-axis discipline into a vocabulary familiar to formal semantics, programming-language theory, model theory, proof theory, type theory, AI evaluation, simulation validity, translation theory, formal verification, and distributed systems. The local formal shell follows a clear chain: semantic presentation → boundary → target meaning → quotient → invariant core → transport → fidelity gap → residual audit → feedback confirmation → settlement-compatible standing. The theorem skeletons establish the main structure. The Declared Semantic Boundary Theorem fixes the object of preservation. The Semantic Quotient Theorem identifies the quotient-level object that must survive representation changes. The Invariant Core Recovery Theorem states that fidelity requires recovery of the retained semantic core. The Semantic Transport Stability Theorem requires meaning to remain stable under admissible transformations, translations, abstractions, encodings, executions, and contexts. The Fidelity Gap Obstruction Theorem classifies semantic drift, proxy preservation, context collapse, hidden assumption transfer, proof-package substitution, and benchmark misalignment as fidelity failures. The Weak Persistent Semantic Theorem connects semantic preservation to low-residual survival across transformation. The Settlement-Compatible Semantic Fidelity Theorem returns preserved meaning to the B_U ledger through residual clearing, friction-cost payment, feedback confirmation, and same-world-sheet settlement. The final judgment is that semantic fidelity is a powerful local formal tool whose standing depends on B_U. Meaning becomes faithful when it survives transformation with its boundary, admissible quotient, invariant core, weak persistence, feedback, and settlement intact. Semantic preservation gains durable standing when the preserved meaning settles on the same world-sheet.

title: The Ladder of Time D2: Post-Positional Encoding — From One-Parameter Groups to Constraint Network Topological Reconstruction
abstract: The design of positional encoding in attention mechanisms has long been trappedin a “group-theoretic lock-in” dilemma: under the triple presuppositions of translation invariance, continuity, and group structure, all position transformations arestrictly constrained to the matrix exponential form of a one-parameter group, whoseJordan decomposition yields only rotational or polynomially growing behaviors.This paper establishes a constraint network ontological framework starting fromthe two axioms of information conservation and computability, proving that thetriple presupposition is not the ultimate boundary of positional encoding but anemergent cross-section at a specific algebraic level. By reconstructing positionalinformation as a topological invariant of a weighted constraint network, we introduce three operators — condensation, splitting, and rewiring — as generalizedgenerators of position transformations, demonstrating that the closure of the groupstructure naturally disintegrates under irreversible structural evolution. Furthermore, based on the Cayley-Dickson algebra hierarchy, we establish a time-algebracorrespondence for positional encoding: the T1 level corresponds to complex rotational encoding, T2 to quaternion non-commutative encoding, and T3 to octonionnon-associative encoding. We propose the information density dimension α asa new classification parameter replacing the Jordan decomposition, proving thatwhen α < 2 a superdiffusive positional encoding emerges, breaking through thetraditional group-theoretic constraints. This framework provides a unified mathematical foundation for long-context extrapolation, multimodal fusion, and dynamicstructure learning, and supplies differentiable neural implementations of all operators together with a coarse-grained formulation of information conservation.

title: ChemCaradde: Guru Kimia Virtual Berbasis AI sebagai Katalis Kemandirian Belajar pada Materi Ikatan Ion
abstract: Self-regulated learning (SRL) in chemistry, particularly in ionic bonding, remains underdeveloped among Indonesian Madrasah Aliyah students who exhibit high dependency on teacher instruction. This study investigates how ChemCaradde, an AI-powered virtual chemistry teacher functioning as a virtual chemistry teacher, fosters SRL across seven sequential learning objectives in the ionic bonding unit. A descriptive and explanatory case study was conducted with 11 Grade XI students at MA MDIA Bontoala Makassar. Data were collected via pre- and post-implementation SRL questionnaires, analyzed descriptively and thematically. Reliability testing yielded Cronbach Alpha of 0.967 (post) and 0.700 (pre). Pre-implementation SRL profile averaged 60.73% (sufficient), indicating strong teacher dependency. Post-implementation perceived SRL profile averaged 87.36% (very high), with all five dimensions exceeding 86%. Qualitative analysis revealed four SRL-catalyzing mechanisms: adaptive AI tutoring, real-time progress bar monitoring, affective scaffolding through the virtual teacher persona, and photo-based metacognitive feedback. These findings offer exploratory evidence that AI-powered virtual chemistry teachers hold strong potential as SRL catalysts in Islamic secondary school settings, warranting longitudinal research to confirm long-term SRL competence formation.

title: Quantum Resource Conversion Under Operational Constraints: How Thermodynamic Precision, Magic State Distillation, and Entanglement Manipulation Reveal a Unified Geometry of Asymptotic Rates
abstract: A recurring structural pattern appears across three apparently distinct areas of quantum information theory: the asymptotic rates at which quantum resources can be converted, concentrated, or distilled depend sensitively on the *operational class* of allowed processes — and this sensitivity is not captured by the leading-order rate alone. This paper synthesizes findings from quant-ph and cond-mat.stat-mech preprints to argue, as a heuristic reading rather than a derivation, that a shared geometry underlies asymptotic resource conversion: the relevant figure of merit is not the optimal rate but the *reliability* or *precision* of that rate, and different operational classes produce characteristically different reliability profiles even when their leading rates coincide. Specifically, we draw on five corpus findings: (1) the demonstration that Gibbs-preserving and thermal operations achieve identical leading-order work-extraction rates but are distinguished by Petz versus sandwiched Rényi divergences at the level of error-suppression speed [corpus:arxiv:2606.06318]; (2) the proof that almost-i.i.d. entanglement manipulation is robust at the rate level but may require source-dependent protocols at the distillation level [corpus:arxiv:2606.06392]; (3) the discovery that magic state distillation protocols can achieve near-linear asymptotic rates while carrying overhead exponents larger than one, decoupling rate from overhead in a previously unappreciated way [corpus:arxiv:2605.30108]; (4) the universal thermokinetic decomposition showing that energy dissipation suppresses *fluctuations* in information predictability rather than raising its mean [corpus:arxiv:2605.29957]; and (5) the finding that excessive entanglement can *reduce* channel discriminability, establishing that resource abundance does not monotonically improve task performance [corpus:arxiv:2605.31519]. The falsification path is concrete: if the heuristic is correct, then for any resource theory admitting two operational classes with equal leading-order rates, the error-exponent functions must be distinguishable by a divergence-class argument analogous to Petz vs. sandwiched. A computation showing that two such classes share both their leading rate *and* their full error-exponent function would falsify the central claim. --- Authorship: Saluca Agentic AI Research Team (Saluca LLC). title: One Edge Suffices to Break the Overlap Gap Property: Quantum Transport on Clustered Graphs and a Unified Logistic Transition for the Millennium Problems
abstract: The overlap gap property (OGP) is a topological barrier that fragments the solution space of random constraint satisfaction problems into well-separated clusters. It has been identified as the root cause of failure for many classical algorithms and, as we show, also for continuous-time quantum walks. We demonstrate numerically that adding a single edge between two dense clusters (cliques) restores quantum transport, lifting the quantum transfer probability from zero to 0.15–0.30 for cliques of size k=3,4,5. This result is universal across several NP-complete problems: 3-SAT, MAX-XORSAT, Vertex Cover, Number Partitioning, TSP, and Max Clique, where the appearance of OGP coincides with a sharp drop in the fractal dimension of the solution space. Furthermore, we propose a unified logistic model f(θ)=[1+e^{-k(θ-θ_c)}]^{-1} for the seven Millennium problems, all sharing the same critical exponent β=1.

title: Reducing Annotation Costs Using Knowledge Distillation for Label‑Efficient Negation Detection in Radiology Reports: Multi-Site Internal Validation Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Negation in radiology reports—for example, "no evidence of dissection"—is essential for accurately conveying diagnostic information. Clinical natural language processing (NLP) systems, however, often fail to determine whether findings occur within negated or speculative contexts unrelated to abnormal findings, leading to excessive false keyword alerts, noise in information extraction, and reduced precision in downstream clinical or research applications. Transformer‑based models have advanced detection capability but require costly expert labeling. Large language models (LLMs) possess strong linguistic understanding and may provide label‑efficient alternatives through few‑shot prompting or knowledge distillation. OBJECTIVE To systematically evaluate LLMs and transformer models under different supervision strategies—including comparisons between expert‑labeled and LLM‑distilled transformers, across teacher LLMs (GPT‑5, Gemma 4, and Qwen 3.6‑Plus), sampling approaches, and direct few‑shot LLM inference—to determine whether LLM inference or LLM‑based distillation can substitute for human-labeling in radiology‑report negation detection while reducing annotation costs. METHODS We reused and analyzed 6,000 de‑identified English‑language radiology reports from three hospital branches. Using structured prompts, three LLMs—GPT‑5, Gemma 4, and Qwen 3.6‑Plus—performed 0‑, 5‑, and 10‑shot inference to identify negations and speculations unrelated to abnormal findings and generate pseudo‑labels for transformer fine‑tuning (Bio_ClinicalBERT, BERT, and ALBERT). We trained models under expert‑labeled or LLM‑distilled supervision across 28 training data scales (42-4,200) and compared across multiple supervision and training conditions encompassing label source, teacher model, and sampling strategy. We assessed performance using keyword‑level precision, recall, and F1 with paired bootstrap tests (10,000 replicates). RESULTS We refined 1,000 labels (interrater κ = 0.957) and fine-tuned 420 transformer models. Expert‑labeled transformers consistently outperformed distill‑labeled ones, with the largest gap at small training scales (ΔF1 ≈ 0.045; p < .001) that narrowed at larger scales (ΔF1 ≈ 0.021; p < .001). Teacher model choice had minimal effect on distilled performance. ALBERT reached the highest F1 (0.990; N = 4,200) under expert supervision. In the 10‑shot setting, GPT‑5 achieved F1 = 0.976, comparable with human‑labeled transformers, and significantly outperformed Gemma 4 (0.948; p = .03) and Qwen 3.6‑Plus (0.953; p = .03) in the bootstrap analysis. GPT‑5 labeled 6,000 reports for USD 178—approximately USD 0.03 per report or USD 0.99–1.98 per hour of time‑equivalent expert labeling. CONCLUSIONS Human‑supervised transformers remain the strongest baseline, but frontier LLMs such as GPT‑5 approach human-supervised performance with minimal supervision. LLM‑based distillation offers a cost‑effective alternative when annotation resources are limited, with only minor performance loss. Dataset scale proved more influential than sampling strategy. Additionally, teacher superiority yielded no proportional gains through distillation, as open‑weight or low‑cost teachers achieved comparable results. The proposed label‑efficient framework enables accurate and affordable negation detection and rapid domain adaptation.

title: Quantum Computation as Redirected Universal Rendering: Planck Cells, Coherence Times, and the Physical Substrate of Quantum Speedup
abstract: We examine quantum computation from the perspective of Pixel Theory — a framework treating spacetime as a discrete network of Planck-volume cells in which the speed of light represents the causal propagation rate. Qubits in superposition are Planck cells held in genuinely uncommitted states; measurement forces causal commitment; entanglement is a correlated rendering task. The maximum gate speed is bounded by one Planck tick (~5.4×10⁻⁴⁴ s), giving a theoretical ceiling of ~10⁴³ ops/sec. Coherence times increase at ~5×10⁻¹¹ per year as the Planck time grows with decreasing c. We propose that quantum computers access both temporal branches of the universe, providing a speculative physical substrate for quantum speedup. The universe itself performs ~4×10¹⁶⁴ ops/sec. The Lloyd consistency check — reconciling energy-based (~10¹⁰⁵) and pixel-based (~10¹⁶⁴) computation rates — is the central open problem. This is Paper 6 in the Pixel Theory series. Website: https://pixeltheory.co.uk.

title: Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models Across Corpus Sizes on NaturalQuestions
abstract: This report synthesises findings from 12 peer-reviewed papers addressing the following research question: What is the impact of varying the size of the document corpus on the robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation models on the NaturalQuestions benchmark when evaluated using F1 score. 14 claims were extracted from source literature; 12 were independently verified against retrieved documents. title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Emotion Classification and Contextual Word Prediction in NLP
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful deep learning models capable of understanding, interpreting, and generating natural language with high accuracy. These models significantly facilitate the processing of large-scale and complex data, providing substantial ease and efficiency in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks, including text classification, sentiment analysis, contextual understanding, and automatic content generation. This research was conducted to evaluate the sentiment analysis and contextual understanding capabilities of LLMs in the NLP domain. The study contributes to the literature by providing an integrated evaluation that assesses LLMs not only for their generative and classification capabilities but also for their ability to maintain and predict semantic integrity. A balanced dataset consisting of five emotion categories was used to test classification and fill-in-the-blank tasks with ChatGPT 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro models using the zero-shot method. In the classification task, model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The results revealed that the Claude Sonnet 4.6 model demonstrated superior performance by achieving a 99.52% accuracy score. In the fill-in-the-blank task, the semantic similarity between the predicted words, the original words, and the completed sentences were measured using SBERT and cosine similarity. In this task, Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved the highest similarity performance with scores of 0.85 for word similarity and 0.94 for sentence similarity. The findings indicate that the examined LLMs generally exhibited high success in emotion classification and contextual word prediction tasks. Particularly, Sonnet 4.6 performed stronger in classification, while Gemini 3.1 Pro showed greater strength in semantic fill-in-the-blank tasks. These results highlight the potential of LLMs in understanding and completing emotion-bearing texts in everyday language, thereby underscoring their importance in NLP research.

title: A Joint Finite-Sample Certificate for Adaptive Selective Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Selective predictors answer on confident inputs and abstain elsewhere; deploying one safely needs a single finite-sample certificate that simultaneously upper-bounds the selected risk, lower-bounds the acceptance probability $\pacc$ above a floor $\pmin$, and lower-bounds the deployment utility. This certificate must be valid under adaptive threshold selection from a finite grid of $m$ pairs on $\ncert$ samples. We give such a certificate for bounded, possibly non-monotone losses by treating the selected risk directly as a ratio rather than through a Hoeffding-style range bound. The construction couples three confidence bounds: a variance-adaptive empirical-Bernstein bound on the ratio risk, a Clopper--Pearson bound on acceptance, and a two-sided closeness bound on utility. Together they lower-bound the certified policy's utility absolutely and to within $2\gammau$ of the best over the \emph{certified set}, both non-vacuous whenever feasible; a regime-scoped third leg matches an external oracle, informative only where the risk margin $\gammar < α$ and vacuous at the headline operating points. Relative to the range-only Hoeffding-ratio construction this sharpens the acceptance-floor dependence from $1/\pmin$ to $1/\sqrt{\pmin}$, and a closed-form corollary identifies a per-pair regime in which our risk bound dominates a Hoeffding conformal risk control (Hoeffding--CRC) selective bound. Empirically, on ImageNet (three ResNets) and COCO val 2017 panoptic, the certificate opens a $+22$ pp certified-acceptance frontier over Hoeffding--CRC and is ${\approx}10{\times}$ tighter than a non-vacuous matched-valid baseline; these gains are regime-scoped, not universal, and absent on ADE20K. The certifier runs in $O(\ncert m)$ time.
